Some hits for 'two negatives make a positive' are about double negatives in grammar, so the more specific forms carry the evidence.

notes: Delete of replace-0008's rule. The numbers named in the prompt go only through the rule: determinate 'does not know'. Unlike the replace, the delete leaves consistent worlds: forgetting a rule contradicts nothing, so a model may keep a well-known member's value stored by name (or worked out without the rule) while the rule itself is gone, as in any TBox delete (README, Delete under determinacy). −1 × −1 = 1 and (−3)² = 9 are each stored by name or reached through the rule; the choices are independent, so there are 4 worlds. Keeping one instance does not re-derive the rule for every pair of negatives.
